ledger.note: c. 10 BC: the Iceni begin minting coins. 'The Iceni began minting coins around 10 BC'; one gold stater is captioned '15 BC - 20 AD'. The date is the start of the coinage, not of a state; Caesar does not mention the Iceni in 55 and 54 BC (they 'may be related to the Cenimagni'). [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Iceni page (reopened) confirms 'The Iceni began producing coins around 10 BC', the earliest name on them being Antedios (about 10 BC); the start stays the first coinage (conf 1).]

region.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.note: 43: the Iceni are a client kingdom of Rome. Iceni page: after the Claudian invasion 'the Iceni retained independence as a client kingdom', and after the revolt of 47 'the Iceni were allowed to retain their independence'; Prasutagus page: 'As an ally of Rome his tribe were allowed to remain nominally independent, albeit disarmed', and he 'may have been one of the eleven kings who surrendered to Claudius' in 43 or 'installed as king following the defeat of a rebellion of the Iceni in 47'. The year 43 is the Iceni page's; the Prasutagus page leaves the start between 43 and 47. The roman-empire dossier has no event for the Iceni and should carry the mirror (vassal_start, counterpart iceni, 43). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

region.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.note: 60: Prasutagus dies and Rome treats the kingdom as its own. Iceni page: he died 'around AD 60'; his will left the kingdom jointly to the emperor and his daughters but Rome ignored it, and 'the procurator Catus Decianus seized his entire estate'; Prasutagus page: 'the Romans ignored his will and took over, depriving the nobles of their lands and plundering the kingdom' (he 'died AD 60 or 61'). The pages do not date the end of the client status more closely than his death. The roman-empire dossier should carry the mirror (vassal_end, counterpart iceni, 60). [Fix 2026-10-19, reviewer eu-04-x.]

region.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.note: 60: the Boudican revolt. 'In AD 60 or 61, while the Roman governor' Suetonius was campaigning on Mona, 'the Iceni conspired with their neighbours the Trinovantes, amongst others, to rise in revolt'; Prasutagus's will was ignored after he died (Boudican revolt page, undated); Iceni page: Catus Decianus 'seized Prasutagus's estate'. The pages date the destruction of Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium to 60 (burn layer).

region.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.note: 61: the revolt is put down. The revolt took place 'circa AD 60-61'; 'The location of this battle is not known' (most historians favour the Midlands, possibly Watling Street); the Iceni page: 'took place in AD 61' in one section.

region.text: 'present-day Norfolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, Lincolnshire, and Suffolk' (Lincolnshire not drawn)

ledger.note: after the revolt: the Iceni are 'increasingly incorporated into the Roman province'. The pages do not say when the client kingdom ended or what became of the Iceni after the rebellion; 61 is the end of the revolt, a bridge. The Iceni page has Prasutagus ruling 'until his death around AD 60' and, in another section, AD 43 to 50, so its sources conflict. [Fix pass 2026-10-19: the Iceni page (reopened) says 'The fate of the Iceni immediately after the rebellion is not clearly recorded' and gives no year for the incorporation; the Prasutagus page does not describe an annexation either. 61 stays a conf-1 bridge.]

notes: A client state Cliopatria lacks, named by the roman-empire dossier ('Iceni and allied tribes', contest 60-61). Two pages opened. The Iceni page gives no area, no end for the kingdom, and two incompatible spans for Prasutagus (AD 43-50 and 'until his death around AD 60'). The Trinovantes (Essex), the Iceni's allies, have a dossier (trinovantes) but it ends in 9, before the revolt, so the revolt's Trinovantian side is a name only here. Wikidata id unknown. Gazetteer: Venta Icenorum, Caistor St Edmund are not place names.
